description: Forge-hardened npm publishing for JS/TS libraries. Multi-runner reproducible-build attestation, OIDC trusted publishing, hard pre-publish gates. Pure bash, zero dependencies.
rules: anvil is a GitHub Action, not an npm package. Consumers reference it via uses: forgesworn/anvil/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
The composite action (uses: forgesworn/anvil@v0) omits the reproducible-build gate. Use the reusable workflow for full protection.
Node version must ship npm >= 11.5.x for OIDC trusted publishing. Node 22 LTS is too old.
Trusted publishing must be configured on npmjs.com pointing at the consumer's repo and workflow file, not at forgesworn/anvil.

The exports-map check (verify-exports.sh) uses jq to walk the full package.json exports tree -- all conditional keys (import/require/types/node/browser/default), nested conditionals, and string shorthand -- plus legacy main/module/types/typings/bin fields. Every leaf path starting with ./ must exist on disk or the release is blocked. No configuration needed; runs automatically. The only input is package-json (default: package.json).

The runtime-only npm audit (verify-audit.sh) runs npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=$AUDIT_LEVEL. The --omit=dev flag excludes devDependencies so only runtime advisories block the release. Configure the threshold via the audit-level input (default: low; valid values: low, moderate, high, critical).

Action-pin auditing (verify-action-pins.sh) scans .github/workflows/*.yml for uses: lines whose @ref is not a 40-char SHA. Default is strict (release blocked on unpinned refs). Set strict-action-pins: false for warn-only mode. forgesworn/anvil is self-exempt by name. Motivated by the tj-actions/changed-files supply-chain attack (March 2025).

Tarball hash stamping: record-tarball.sh packs with normalised mtimes and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, records filename/size/sha256/sha512 to tarball.meta. After publish, update-release.sh stamps an Artefact Integrity block into the GitHub Release body with the hashes and a curl+shasum verify recipe, and uploads the .tgz as a release asset. Consumers get two independent sources for the bytes (npm registry + GitHub Releases).

SLSA provenance: driven by publishConfig.provenance: true in package.json (NOT --provenance CLI flag; npm 11.6+ breaks OIDC with explicit flag). Requires id-token: write permission. npm exchanges the GitHub OIDC token for a Sigstore certificate and attaches the attestation to the registry entry. Consumers verify via npm audit signatures or the Provenance badge on npmjs.com. Troubleshoot with debug: true input.
